newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Hebron deal "not guaranteed".
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Hebron deal "not guaranteed".

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday there was no guarantee Israel and the PLO would seal a Hebron deal at his midnight summit with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
"The chance that we will finish this evening exists but it is not guaranteed," Netanyahu told reporters in Jerusalem.
Israeli and PLO negotiators were set to resume talks in Jerusalem ahead of the summit to remove obstacles blocking Israel's long overdue withdrawal from 80 percent of Hebron in the West Bank.
Earlier on Tuesday, Ross announced the two leaders would meet at the Erez crossing between Israel and Gaza at midnight (2200 GMT) in efforts to complete the deal after months of negotiations.
"I'm convinced we can seal this agreement in a very short time with goodwill from the other side," Netanyahu said.

Hebron, a West Bank flashpoint, is home to 400 militant Jewish settlers and 100,000 Arabs. It was to be handed over to the Palestinians last March but violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June delayed the pullback.
